html:
A rechargeable battery that moves lithium ions between two electrodes. In 1985 the Japanese chemist Akira Yoshino built the first practical version, with a carbon anode and a lithium cobalt oxide cathode.

It built on earlier work. In the 1970s M. Stanley Whittingham made the first lithium battery that could be recharged, and in 1980 John Goodenough found the cobalt oxide cathode. Yoshino's design was safe enough to sell, and Sony put the first ones on the market in 1991.

These batteries store a lot of energy for their weight. They made laptops and mobile phones possible, and later electric cars and storage for solar and wind power. Most are now made in China, South Korea and Japan, and demand for lithium, cobalt and nickel has made mines in Chile, Australia and Congo important. Goodenough, Whittingham and Yoshino shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2019.
